note: Book II (Sadhana Pada) of Patanjali's Yoga Sutras, Johnston translation with commentary. Probes target ashtanga / kleshas / yamas / niyamas, distinctive to book-02 among the four books.

queries.query: Patanjali's ashtanga scheme laying out the eight successive limbs of the yoga path that a practitioner must work through in strict order, starting with ethical restraints and moving up to deep absorption
queries.note: Sutra 29 enumerates the eight means as 'Commandments, Rules, right Poise, right Control of the life-force, Withdrawal, Attention, Meditation, Contemplation' — I paraphrased away that specific list and used the reader-honest anchors 'ashtanga' and 'eight limbs' plus the 'follow in order' framing.

queries.query: the five kleshas or root afflictions Patanjali names as the sources of bondage — spiritual ignorance, ego-identification, craving, aversion, and the tenacious clinging to continued existence
queries.note: Sutra 3 renders the five as 'the darkness of unwisdom, self-assertion, lust, hate, attachment'. I used the standard klesha names (ignorance/ego/craving/aversion/clinging) instead of the chunk's idiosyncratic vocabulary; 'kleshas' and 'afflictions' are reader-honest anchors.

queries.query: the yamas, Patanjali's five universal ethical restraints binding on everyone regardless of birth or circumstance — refraining from harm, deceit, taking what is not given, sexual excess, and grasping for possessions
queries.note: Sutra 30 lists 'non injury, truthfulness, abstaining from stealing, from impurity, from covetousness'; Sutra 31 stresses they hold across all races, places, times. I paraphrased the list into my own words and used 'yamas' as a reader-honest anchor.

queries.query: Patanjali's rule for asana, the bodily seat or posture used in yoga: the position taken for meditation should be stable and at ease, held steadily yet with no strain, so the finer life-currents can flow
queries.note: Sutras 46-47 on 'right poise' (asana): 'Right poise must be firm and without strain... gained by steady and temperate effort.' Replaces an earlier ahimsa probe (Sutra 35) that could not surface book-02 honestly — its harmlessness content collided with cross-tradition nonviolence, and a siddhi framing pulled book-03. 'Asana' and 'posture' are reader-honest anchors; I reworded 'firm and without strain' rather than lifting it.

queries.query: why is ordinary worldly life inherently unsatisfying, and can suffering be headed off before it even arises
queries.note: Sutras 15-16 (all personal life is misery, waxing and waning; pain to be warded off before it comes). The diagnosis of dukkha and its pre-emption is shared with Buddhism and Stoic thought. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: how does a seeker learn to steadily tell apart what is eternal and real from what is fleeting and temporary
queries.note: Sutra 26 on unwavering discernment between the eternal and the temporal — the commentary itself ties it to Vedanta, Plato, and St. Paul, so the same question runs through several traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.
